clue.text: Caddie that becomes rogue after such decline?

definitions.text: Caddie that becomes rogue after such decline?

parts.words: Caddie that becomes rogue after such decline?
parts.note: if the last three letters of the golfer's helper fade out, what is left is CAD, a rogue; the phrase for fading out is the answer

explanation.surface: A golf caddie goes to the bad after some fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CADDIE and let its DIE drop out: you are left with CAD, a rogue. The clue asks for the phrase meaning that kind of fading.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade gradually into silence or nothing is to decline, the phrasal verb's usual sense.

clue.text: Old Etonians perhaps finding university in Milan different

indicators.note: made different, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Former pupils of an English public school end up studying in Italy instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' is the anagram signal working on U plus MILAN. Old Etonians are former pupils of Eton, a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Former pupils of any school are its graduates, and Old Etonians are an example of such former students.

clue.text: Vague, dizzy, having scratched good part of the eye

indicators.note: a dizzy head spins, so the remaining letters are spun into a new order
scratched as in withdrawn from a race, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone feels vague and dizzy after scratching an eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having scratched' removes G from VAGUE, leaving VAUE; 'dizzy' then rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigmented middle layer of the eyeball, comprising iris, choroid and ciliary body, has this anatomical name.

clue.text: Paul's uppermost netting catches one fish

indicators.note: in a down clue the uppermost letter of a word is its first
the netting holds the next piece within it, as a net catches

parts.note: lace is an open, net-like fabric
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Paul's top net hauls in a single fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppermost' gives P from Paul's; 'catches' puts I inside LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish of European waters, popular in British fish and chip shops, it is a familiar example of a fish.

clue.text: Prune consumed during latest trouble? Patient might need this soon

indicators.note: the cutting word is swallowed up within the abbreviation for the latest news

parts.note: SP is slang for the latest information, as in 'what's the SP?'
to lop is to prune
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone who ate prunes recently is in trouble, and a patient will soon need the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed during' signals the container; SP is British slang for the lowdown or latest news. The surface hints at the laxative effect of prunes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket for bodily waste, used by bedridden invalids, is something a patient may need.

clue.text: Bottle taken travelling through centre of Delhi

parts.note: via means by way of, travelling through a place

indicators.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word Delhi is taken

explanation.surface: A bottle carried by someone passing through the heart of Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' picks L, the third letter of Delhi.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass container for medicine or perfume is a kind of little bottle.

clue.text: Extremist in despicable wickedness?

indicators.note: the extreme, outermost, letter at the start of despicable is taken

parts.note: evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: An extremist steeped in despicable wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremist in' takes D, the first letter of despicable, and EVIL follows. The whole clue also describes the answer, an extreme figure of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the embodiment of wickedness, the ultimate extremist in evil.

clue.text: Woman rejected beer during a date

indicators.note: sent back, so the whole phrase that follows is read backwards

parts.note: ale is beer
in means during

explanation.surface: A woman turns down a beer while out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole string round, not just the beer; D is the usual abbreviation for date.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's forename, so it stands for a woman in the usual crossword way.

clue.text: Scriptural character, one existing on bread abroad

indicators.note: one piece lives on, follows after, the other in the charade

parts.note: the lev is the Bulgarian currency, and bread is slang for money
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A biblical figure who survives on foreign bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'existing on' puts I after LEV; bread is slang for money, and the lev is Bulgaria's.
explanation.definitionFit: The third son of Jacob in Genesis, ancestor of the Levites, is a scriptural character.

clue.text: Music maker playing PM's place with zero backing

parts.note: V for versus, as when one team is playing another
No 10 Downing Street is the Prime Minister's home; the 10 is written as the letters I and O

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for zero is reversed

parts.note: nil means zero, as in a football score

explanation.surface: A musician performs at the Prime Minister's residence while the score stays at nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prime Minister lives at No 10 Downing Street, and the figures 1 and 0 are read as letters; 'backing' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument played with a bow is one example of something that makes music.

clue.text: Soldiers' great passion to find source of a 7 Across

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, with the possessive S
a mania is an overwhelming enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Troops' fervour leads them to find where a devil comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is Britain's Territorial Army of volunteer reserve soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The island state of Australia is home to the Tasmanian devil, so it is where that creature comes from.

clue.text: Little devil, third in show, brought in Bible for ad libbing

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the abbreviation for the Bible

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: the third letter of show is taken

explanation.surface: A mischievous performer inserts a bit of scripture into a show while making it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third in' takes O from show; 'brought in' puts it inside RV, the Revised Version of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for improvisation: performing without a script, the comic sense of making it up on the spot.

clue.text: US wood-cutter inside it reversed vehicle

indicators.note: the cutter goes inside the other two letters
the little word it is read backwards

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: An American lumberjack's axe gets stuck inside an upturned vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' applies only to 'it'; 'inside' signals the container, and ax is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab you hire for a journey is a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Unclothed celeb entertains football team outcast

indicators.note: the stripped word hosts, holds within it, the next piece
stripped of its outer letters, so only the inside of celeb is kept

parts.note: XI is eleven, the number in a football side

explanation.surface: A naked celebrity hosts a football team, a social outcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unclothed' strips the outer letters from celeb; 'entertains' signals the container. A football side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: One banished from their homeland is an outcast in the literal sense.

clue.text: Sick around Iowa — it relates to the hip area there

definitions.text: it relates to the hip area there

indicators.note: the word for sick goes around the state abbreviation

parts.note: ill means sick
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: An ill traveller in Iowa has a complaint about the hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container. The definition is descriptive: the word is an adjective for the hip bone region.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilium is the large upper bone of the pelvis, so this adjective concerns that hip region.

clue.text: Ladies regularly gathering vote for alliance

indicators.note: the picked letters gather in, enclose, the mark
every second letter of Ladies is taken

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Women meeting regularly to collect votes for a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks AIS from Ladies; 'gathering' puts X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime pact of Germany, Italy and Japan was called this, a political alliance.

clue.text: Ian acts strangely with partner, like a 7 Across

indicators.note: behaving strangely, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Ian behaves oddly alongside his partner, quite fiendishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges IANACTS into SATANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like Satan, the devil of 7 Across, is the adverb's literal sense.

clue.text: Charlie Tango flies through Irish air like a bird?

indicators.note: the pieces travel through, sit inside, the Irish word

parts.note: aer is Irish for air, as in the airline Aer Lingus
a charlie is a fool, a twit
T is Tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A pilot's call sign zooms through the Irish sky like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Tango looks like radio code, but Charlie is a fool and only Tango is the NATO letter. 'flies through' signals the container; Aer Lingus is Ireland's airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds twitter, so being in a twittering, excited state is literally bird-like.

clue.text: Exonerated old party grabbed by first-rate journalist

indicators.note: the party is held inside the term for first-rate

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in letters
Lib is short for the Liberal Party, the old British party
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A former political party seized by a top reporter is cleared of blame.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as AI, means first-rate; the Liberal Party, LIB, merged into today's Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Given an excuse showing one was elsewhere, so cleared of an accusation.

clue.text: Turner — captivating artist, here near Adriatic

indicators.note: holding captive, so the singer's name holds the artist inside

parts.note: Tina Turner, the singer
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Turner, the painter, enthralled by a place on the Adriatic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner seems to be the painter J. M. W. Turner but is the singer; 'captivating' signals the container. RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania's capital stands near the Adriatic coast, a city located in that region.

clue.text: Emergency transportation one's seen, by rail, organised daily

indicators.note: arranged into order, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: I is one, and one's here means one is
FT is the Financial Times, a daily paper

explanation.surface: Someone seen by the railway helps run an emergency evacuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges I and RAIL into AIRLI; the Financial Times is a British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving people or supplies by aircraft, especially in a crisis, is emergency transport.

clue.text: Panorama that is seen inside car

indicators.note: these letters appear within the car's badge

parts.note: VW is a Volkswagen
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A sweeping vista enjoyed from inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen inside' signals the container; ie is Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide scene of landscape, a vista, is a panorama.

clue.text: Songstress Anna caught 6 dancing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: letters dancing about are rearranged

parts.note: 6 refers to 6 Across, the small bottle

explanation.surface: A singer caught dancing at number six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges VIAL, the answer to 6 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Calvi is an English singer-songwriter, so her surname completes the name.

clue.text: Head of camp to 'old light

indicators.note: the first letter of camp is taken

parts.note: hold with its H dropped, Cockney style; its synonym handle loses its H the same way

explanation.surface: A camp leader is told to keep an old lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old is hold spoken without its H; handle means hold, so it too drops its H to give ANDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a wick is a source of light.

clue.text: Fervent prima donna's upset

parts.note: a diva is a prima donna; 's means is

explanation.surface: The fiery opera star is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DIVA around.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and enthusiastic is the same as fervent, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Adopt cuckoo, bird unable to fly back

parts.note: a cuckoo is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: the bird's name is read back to front

parts.note: the emu is a flightless bird

explanation.surface: Take on a cuckoo, a bird that cannot fly back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EMU into UME.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a manner or role is to adopt it.

clue.text: Devil-may-care worker breaks retiring present

indicators.note: breaks into, so the worker sits inside
going backwards, so the word is reversed

an ant is a worker

explanation.surface: A reckless employee disrupts a retirement presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses only the word for present; 'breaks' signals the container. Ant is the crossword's usual worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless and unrestrained behaviour is careless of consequences, a devil-may-care attitude.

clue.text: Independently, Yankee tucks into scraps — little devil

indicators.note: the letter is tucked inside the word for scraps

an elf is a mischievous little sprite

explanation.surface: An American tucks into leftovers on his own with a small imp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' places Y inside BITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something alone and unaided is doing it independently.

clue.text: Page 3 girls perhaps discussed alcoholic drink

indicators.note: talked about, so the word is the one heard

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Tabloid models are talked about over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 girls were topless models in The Sun, a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of women is a bevy, the collective noun, so a set of models fits as an example.

clue.text: Read about stuntman, when tied to 7 Across

indicators.note: turned about, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reading up about a stuntman with a devilish streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges READ. Joined to devil it makes daredevil.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless stunt performer, so this word joined to devil names the stuntman.

clue.text: 7 Across climbing drew breath

indicators.note: climbing goes backwards up the word, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: the answer to 7 Across, Satan's title

explanation.surface: The devil climbs up and takes a breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' is a down-clue reversal used in an across clue, so it simply turns the word around.
explanation.definitionFit: To have drawn breath is to have been alive, existed.

clue.text: Fergie originally involved in curtailing lots of Red Devils

indicators.note: the initial is wrapped up in the shortened word
cutting off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: much means lots

indicators.note: the first letter of Fergie is taken

explanation.surface: Fergie, involved early, keeps cutting a lot of the Red Devils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailing' takes H off MUCH; 'originally' gives F. Fergie is Sir Alex Ferguson, long-time Manchester United manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester United Football Club is nicknamed the Red Devils.
